newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. refugee aid train attacked in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. refugee aid train attacked in Zaire.

text.p: The United Nations suspended operations in Rwandan Hutu refugee camps south of Kisangani in Zaire on Monday after a train carrying food to the camps was attacked, an aid official said.

The train carrying 119 tonnes of food aid for malnourished and exhausted refugees was attacked overnight near the military barracks at Lula, seven km (four miles) south of Kisangani, said Carlos Haddad of the U.N. World Food Programme.
The incident was the latest in a series to hamper U.N. operations south of Kisangani.
Residents surrounded the train despite the presence of soldiers who shot in the air, and the train crew fled into the jungle. It was not clear if the train was looted.
"The food is very important. This food was destined for Kilometre 41 (Biaro camp)," Haddad told reporters.
He said there were no further details and U.N. staff had yet to visit the site.
Around 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees languish at Biaro and Kasese camps south of Kisangani where they arrived in March after a five-month trek through the jungle.
Protests from local authorities over a cholera outbreak at Kasese camp have forced the U.N. refugee agency to postpone indefinitely a plan to start repatriating refugees by air.
